newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two bombs in northern Spain.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs in northern Spain.

text.p: Two bombs exploded in the northern city of Gijon early on Saturday and were said by a telephone caller to have been planted by Basque separatists. Police said no one was injured.
ETA guerrillas have not previously attacked in Asturias, more than 200 km (125 miles) west of the Basque Region, but 17 of its members are serving prison sentences in the area.
A 20-kg (44-lb) bomb exploded in front of Gijon's new palace of justice, leaving a metre- (yard-) deep hole in the ground and shattering the windows of a car showroom.
A smaller bomb exploded earlier outside a pharmacy owned by the husband of Paz Fernandez Felgueroso, a former secretary of state for penal affairs.
A woman phoned police to warn about the explosions. She said the separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) took responsibility.
The central government's representative in the northern region of Asturias, Fernando Fernandez Noval, said it was likely that the larger bomb had been planted by a roving ETA commando.

Four people were slightly injured in a car-bomb attack on Friday against Civil Guard barracks in the north-eastern town of Bunuel. Local politicians blamed the attack on ETA. Some 800 people have died in ETA attacks since 1968.
